methodology: The original research topic and the generated technical specification were decomposed into atomic information units based on individual requirements, features, behaviors, constraints, and state transitions. Each atomic unit is designed to be independent, self-contained, technically specific, unambiguous, and implementable as a single requirement. For the original research topic, the decomposition focused on extracting the core functionalities and constraints described in the problem statement. For the generated technical specification, the decomposition focused on extracting the described logic functions, module behaviors, and signal flow.
mindtraced_atomic_units: Lemmings are modeled using a finite state machine.
Lemmings can be in walk_left state.
Lemmings can be in walk_right state.
Lemmings can be in falling state.
Lemmings can be in digging state.
Lemmings can be in splattered state.
areset resets the Lemming to walk_left state.
If bump_left is 1, Lemming switches to walk_right.
If bump_right is 1, Lemming switches to walk_left.
If both bump_left and bump_right are 1, Lemming switches direction.
bump inputs are ignored while falling.
When ground becomes 0, Lemming enters falling state and aaah output becomes 1.
If ground remains 0, Lemming continues to fall.
When ground becomes 1 again, Lemming stops falling and resumes walking in the same direction.
bump inputs are ignored when ground becomes 0 in the same cycle.
bump inputs are ignored when ground reappears while still falling.
Lemming can start digging if ground is 1 and dig input is 1.
Lemming continues digging until ground becomes 0.
digging output is 1 while digging.
bump inputs are ignored while digging.
dig input is ignored when Lemming is not walking on the ground or is already falling.
If Lemming falls for more than 20 clock cycles and then ground becomes 1, Lemming will splatter.
In splatter state, walk_left, walk_right, aaah, and digging outputs become 0 and remain 0 until areset is asserted.
clk is the clock input.
areset is the asynchronous reset input.
bump_left is the input indicating a bump on the left.
bump_right is the input indicating a bump on the right.
ground is the input indicating the presence of ground.
dig is the input to initiate digging.
walk_left is the output indicating the Lemming is walking left.
walk_right is the output indicating the Lemming is walking right.
aaah is the output indicating the Lemming is falling.
digging is the output indicating the Lemming is digging.
spec_atomic_units: combinational logic determines walk_left, walk_right, aaah, and digging based on current state and inputs.
Logic prioritizes outputs as follows: aaah (falling) > digging > direction change (based on bumps).
splatter condition overrides all other outputs, setting them to 0.
aaah is asserted when ground is 0 and splatter is not asserted.
digging is asserted when dig is asserted AND ground is asserted and splatter is not asserted.
Direction change logic determines whether the Lemming should walk left or right based on bump_left and bump_right.
Direction change logic is only active if the Lemming is not falling and not digging.
walk_left_prev and walk_right_prev are inputs representing the previous walking direction.
Falling logic has the highest priority, followed by the digging logic, and then the direction change logic.
ground signal is used in both the falling and digging logic.
bump_left and bump_right signals are only used in the direction change logic.
critical path is likely to be the path that determines the walk_left and walk_right outputs.
AND gates can be shared between the digging logic and the output multiplexing logic.
Buffers can be inserted in the falling and digging logic paths to equalize the delay with the direction change logic path.
Multiplexers are used to select the appropriate outputs based on the falling, digging, and direction change conditions.
Outputs are prioritized as follows: Splatter > Falling > Digging > Direction Change.
aaah = !ground & !splatter
digging = dig & ground & !splatter
bump_condition = bump_left | bump_right
new_direction = bump_condition
walk_left_new = (walk_right_prev & new_direction) | (walk_left_prev & !new_direction)
walk_right_new = (walk_left_prev & new_direction) | (walk_right_prev & !new_direction)
walk_left = (walk_left_new & !aaah & !digging) & !splatter
walk_right = (walk_right_new & !aaah & !digging) & !splatter
Falling Module implements the aaah output based on the ground input.
Digging Module implements the digging output based on the ground and dig inputs.
Direction Change Module implements the walk_left_new and walk_right_new signals based on the bump_left, bump_right, walk_left_prev, and walk_right_prev inputs.
Output Multiplexing Module selects the final walk_left and walk_right outputs based on the aaah, digging, walk_left_new, and walk_right_new signals.
Splatter Module forces all outputs to 0 if the splatter input is asserted.
ground, dig, bump_left, bump_right, walk_left_prev, and walk_right_prev signals enter the combinational logic.
Falling Module generates the aaah signal.
Digging Module generates the digging signal.
Direction Change Module generates the walk_left_new and walk_right_new signals.
Output Multiplexing Module selects the final walk_left and walk_right signals based on the aaah, digging, walk_left_new, and walk_right_new signals.
Splatter Module forces all outputs to 0 if splatter is asserted.
aaah, digging, walk_left, and walk_right signals are the outputs of the combinational logic.
critical path is likely to be through the Output Multiplexing Module.
walk_left_prev and walk_right_prev are external inputs representing the previous walking direction.
splatter is an external input indicating that the Lemming has splattered.
The design does not include any memory elements. It is purely combinational.
areset input asynchronously resets the state machine to the walking left state.
clk input clocks all state transitions.
bump_left and bump_right inputs cause a change in walking direction on the next clock edge if the Lemming is walking.
ground input, when transitioning from 1 to 0, causes the Lemming to fall on the next clock edge.
When ground transitions from 0 to 1 after a fall of > 20 cycles, the Lemming splatters.
dig input, when 1 and the Lemming is walking on the ground, causes the Lemming to dig until ground becomes 0.
critical path involves the fall counter.
reset signal areset asynchronously resets the entire state machine, overriding all other inputs.
outputs walk_left, walk_right, aaah, and digging are Moore-type outputs, meaning they depend only on the current state and change synchronously with the clock.

state machine requires at least three registers: one to store the walking direction, one to indicate if the Lemming is falling/digging/splattered, and one to count the number of clock cycles the Lemming has been falling.
walking direction register is updated on the rising edge of clk when bump_left or bump_right is asserted and the Lemming is walking.
falling register is set when ground transitions from 1 to 0.
fall counter increments on each rising edge of clk while ground is 0.
splatter state is entered when the fall counter exceeds 20 and ground transitions from 0 to 1.
All state transitions are implemented using non-blocking assignments within a clocked always block.
